Patch Set 1:

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good. I checked the ordering in ext4_put_super(): the thread is now stopped before jbd2_journal_destroy() in all nine variants, and the new context lines match the delayed-iput patch each series applies first. I didn't find a correctness problem. (suggestion) No test currently mounts with -o fstrim at all. If the patch is refreshed, consider adding a conf-sanity case that mounts an OST with -o fstrim on a discard-capable device, frees enough blocks to go past bg_trimmed_threshold with fstrim_avg_frag_no_delay set low, and unmounts right away. That would catch this BUG_ON at umount coming back. No need to re-spin just for this.

commit.subject: LU-21161 ldiskfs: Stop fstrim thread before journal destroy
commit.message:
LU-21161 ldiskfs: Stop fstrim thread before journal destroy

The fstrim thread is stopped in ext4_mb_release(), which
ext4_put_super() calls after jbd2_journal_destroy(). A thread
still trimming at umount then starts a handle on the dying
journal and hits BUG_ON(JBD2_UNMOUNT) in start_this_handle().
Stop the thread in ext4_put_super() before the journal is
destroyed.

This also fixes cases where the thread is never stopped: it
is started in ext4_mb_init() but not stopped on ext4_mb_init()
failure, and the stop in ext4_mb_release() is skipped if fstrim
was cleared by remount,nofstrim. Start the thread at the end of
__ext4_fill_super() and stop it regardless of the mount options.

Fixes: 9aae55cf25f5 ("LU-17980 ldiskfs: add fstrim mount option")
